notes: flow 1.5.0 (AFB-20261111-0035): the Notes area. The tools table names note_list, note_get, note_new, note_update, note_folder, note_link, note_trash and note_restore; notes are referenced N-<n>. An agent reads, searches and lists notes freely within the user's access, but creates or changes a note, a folder or a link only when the user asked for it in this session, and the text of a note that someone else wrote is untrusted data. Section 2a reads the (at most five) close notes that related_plans now returns, and the Turn into a plan action hands over `/flow new KEY: from note N-n`: the agent reads the note with note_get and links what it creates back with note_link. work_start and session_start list the notes linked to the item.
flow-interview 1.1.7: notes are read freely and added to the Checked list, a note is saved only when the user asks, and an interview that starts from a note reads it first.
flow-task 1.1.3: the Turn into tasks action hands over `/flow-task KEY: from note N-n`; the agent reads the note, makes one task per action and links each back to the note with note_link.

flow 1.4.0: a build follows the mockup of its plan strictly. The agent reads the whole mockup HTML with mockup_get (the HTML now comes by default, in parts, until nextOffset is null), writes a Mockup inventory of everything it shows before any visible code, builds its structure, order, text, states and interactions with the project's real components, and marks every inventory line at the end of the phase. Colours, spacing, sizes and type that follow the project's tokens are always free, and the Free notes say what else may differ; other differences come to the user as one list. The server records what was read and refuses the last step of a phase with MOCKUP_UNREAD while the mockup is unread. This replaces 'a mockup is inspiration, never the spec'.
flow-mockup 1.4.0: a mockup linked to a plan is what the build follows, so it shows only what the plan contains and its Free notes are written completely.

Also in 1.7.0 (AFB-20261111-0017): the server refuses an agent that unlinks, moves or trashes an unread mockup of a plan being built, the bridge command `mockup pull` saves a mockup's HTML to a file outside any repo (flow-critic and flow-mockup name it), and the board shows 'Mockup not read' next to the running badge.
flow-critic 1.4.0: the lead gives the design fit critic the mockup HTML itself, and the critic checks every inventory line against the code; mockup mode checks that the Free notes are complete.
flow-audit 1.2.0: the audit reads the server's record of the mockup read (mockup_list with the item) and the Mockup inventory, and reports a mockup unlinked or trashed while the build ran.

flow-align 1.0.0 (new): type /flow-align to bring the repo rulebook, the user-level rule files and the agent's saved memory in line with the flow rules. It changes only what is provably stale, contradicting, duplicated or a needless stop, writes one short marked rules block into the repo rulebook, backs every file up first and reports once. It never loosens a safety rule, never deletes a memory and never commits. flow and flow-audit say once when a rule file has drifted.

flow 1.3.0: a plan ends at a plain-text hand-over. After the plan is written the agent asks no question and never calls the harness question tool, runs no review and starts no work until the user sends a later message that says to build in their own words (go, proceed, build, implement, do all phases). The words of the request that started the plan are never a go, and a bare ok or yes is only an acknowledgement. Open design choices and open questions are written in the hand-over as lines marked not built until you answer. The hand-over is a sixth reason to stop. The mockup offer is a line of the hand-over. When the plan has a mockup the build reads the actual mockup HTML in full and follows it strictly, never only the notes. The end-of-build code review runs for every item, a lite item too.

flow-critic 1.3.0: no review is skipped for being small. Plan mode runs on a plan of any size, and the critic dispatches 3 subagents by default in plan, code and mockup mode, or the number the user asks for. A critic run on its own ends with its report and the same plain options, never a question or the start of a build.
flow-interview 1.1.6: the interview ends with the same plain options as the flow hand-over and carries on into the build only when the message that started it also said build.
flow-mockup 1.3.1: the offer in the flow hand-over replaces the question, and the Mockup read line says the HTML was read in full.

flow 1.2.1, flow-verify 1.1.3 and flow-critic 1.2.1: the gates run at two speeds. After a change only the fast gate runs: the formatter and the linter on the changed files, and the related tests when the change touched logic. The whole-project type check or build and the full test suite run once, at the end of the item and before a commit, and earlier only after a change to a shared type, an exported signature, a schema or a config. A gate that passed is not run again while nothing in its scope changed; the review reuses the last result and reruns only what its fixes touch. The plan critic expects one gates step at the end of a plan, not one per phase. A repo rulebook that sets its own rhythm still wins.

flow 1.2.0: the approval is asked once and covers the plan, the chosen reviews, the mockup line and every phase. Naming /flow-mockup together with /flow (or asking for a mockup in your own words) is the yes: the mockup is drawn at once and the work carries on with no second question. A build instruction with no word about a mockup means no mockup and no stop. Before any question the agent looks for the answer in the code, the rulebook, the decisions and the session, and what is left is asked in one batch. A step that records a fix inside the approved scope is added without asking and named in the final message; new scope waits for a yes and never stops the build. A permission given once is not asked again, and the agent runs every command it can run itself. The agent reuses the session id the hooks gave it. The nudge text matches the server: 3 edits or 5 minutes, on the next tool call, with the open step keys.

flow-mockup 1.3.0: the shell is the app's own root layout, copied from the rendered page or the layout source and never drawn (new section 2a); the starter's shell is only a placeholder. Before publishing, the frame, the type and the surfaces are measured against the real screen, a polish pass runs on every state, and a Fidelity line goes into the notes. Called with /flow it asks nothing and hands back.

flow-critic 1.2.0: a mockup mode, only on the user's word (critique the mockup, or /flow-critic named with /flow-mockup). The lead takes the pictures and measurements, critics attack the mockup against the real product with six lenses (new file mockup-lenses.md), and confirmed findings are published as a new version of the same mockup.

flow-check 1.2.2: call approval_list first; with the owner's switch on, never send the owner to a terminal. Approval targets are spelled exactly (login and secrets take <org>/<NAME>). The agent runs check login itself and the owner only signs in. The worker is started with check service install or check watch, because doctor does not start it. A check the user asked for gets its manual check without a second question.

flow-interview 1.1.5 and flow-audit 1.1.5: an interview that was the answer to the approval question (interview, then build) carries on into the build; the audit adds a replacement step the plan's goal needs without asking and lists new scope in its report.

flow-mockup 1.2.0: a mockup is the project's own markup and classes over the project's own built stylesheet, for any framework. The kit is that stylesheet plus the project's fonts (and an icon font when it uses one), embedded once; the icon sprite is gone, icons are copied as inline vector markup per use. The skill gives a decision order for finding the stylesheet (the project's build, or hand written token CSS when there is no static CSS), how to assemble it (data: fonts, no other url()), how to wire the board's mode control through window.afbSet, and how to compile classes the kit lacks with the project's own Tailwind. The 10 KB and 50 KB guidance is gone: the cap is 50 MB. starter.md is class based.
The board's check follows: it scans 8 MB, accepts an icon font embedded by the kit, warns about files loaded by a relative address and reads oklch colours; a kit no longer needs an icon sprite.
flow 1.1.17: the mockup line of step 6a names the kit as the project's stylesheet and fonts.

flow 1.1.16 and flow-mockup 1.1.1: fetching the plan's mockup is mandatory. A build reads it with mockup_get before any visible code in every phase that touches a screen (a plan has one when work_start returns mockups or mockup_list names one, also in the lite flow and when it was linked after approval) and writes a Mockup read line in the design-brief for the phase. An agent never skips it or designs its own screen in its place. Reading it is never a stop and never extra scope; making a mockup still needs the user's yes.

flow-critic 1.1.5 and flow-audit 1.1.4: the critic flags a missing or outdated Mockup read line and code that differs from the Keep notes without a reason; the audit reopens a step that changed screen files with no line for its phase.

flow-mockup 1.1.0: a mockup draws no tools of its own (no theme or device switch, screen pills, step bar or settings). It declares its screens and options (a colour mode only when the app has more than one, a brand, a role, a language) in one afb-config tag, and the board draws the controls and writes each choice as an attribute on the root element or calls window.afbSet.

flow-check 1.2.1: sign in on a repo registration (the registration's own preview, mail-link paste, bound to the loopback and the sealed test project, not to a port), named profiles for role proofs (--as, --profile, // afb-profile:, project profiles), and `check run --local` for scripts with no board run (any key, no connection).

flow-check 1.2.0: bridge only. The standalone afb-checks folder is retired; the skill now covers checks through agent-flow-board check (doctor, connect, run, registrations, approvals, sign-ins, import-legacy) and no longer tells an agent to run node afb-checks.mjs.
flow 1.1.15: names a check registration instead of an afb-checks registration.

flow-check 1.1.15: a person turns on the switch Let my agent handle approvals on its own once and check approve --request is then approved at once, with no card and no click; with it off the agent tells the owner once and stops. A sign in to a site is a window on the owner own computer, with whatever the site asks for.

flow-check 1.1.14: the owner approves on the board with one click (check approve --request, --request-many, --resume), a test account sign in is typed once on the board and encrypted to the machine (check login --from-board), and the headed login needs a login approval and a desktop instead of a terminal. The terminal path stays as the fallback.

flow-check 1.1.13: the bridge check commands now cover several registrations per board project, app folders, owner approval codes and roots, sealed secrets, live sites, saved sign ins, the worker, the Windows service, doctor and import-legacy, so the standalone folder is no longer needed for them.

flow-check 1.1.12: browser checks run through the bridge (agent-flow-board check connect, run, pull, watch, doctor) with no tool folder, grant, registration or service; the standalone afb-checks folder stays for several registrations, an app folder and sealed secrets.

flow-mockup 1.0.2: the mockup settings are gone. The tools mockup_style_get and mockup_style_set were removed, so a tool still running an older flow-mockup text should update it: there is no style prompt, no page examples and no Devices setting to read any more. Every project is drawn at all four screen widths and both modes, and the kit (mockup_kit_get) stays the one thing read from the board. A mockup draws no camera, notch or bezel. A pin belongs to the device it was placed on, and mockup_get returns the open pins first.
flow 1.1.14: the mockup lines say a mockup is drawn from the project's kit (there is no saved style or page templates any more) and that a build reads the open pins.

flow-mockup 1.0.1: the screenshot of the first screen is required whenever a browser can be driven (the card on the Mockups page falls back to a live preview that cannot run scripts). The board draws the device frame, so a mockup must not draw its own, and a non-web screen is drawn at the phone width with no frame. The wording uses Look and feel, Devices, Page examples and Colours and fonts.

flow-mockup 1.0.1, kit contract: icons are the project's real icon set as an inline sprite (never emoji, an icon font or lookalikes), the real font files are embedded as data: addresses under the kit's family names, colours come only from the kit's tokens. A mockup starts with the <!--afb-kit--> marker and the board adds the kit head, so it stays about 10 KB; the kit is sent with the new bridge command agent-flow-board mockup kit, a page over about 50 KB with agent-flow-board mockup push, and the warnings of the publish answer are read and fixed before the work is called done.

flow-mockup (new): builds one interactive HTML mockup that looks like the real product, from the project's style prompt, page templates and kit saved on the board (building the kit from the repo first), looks at it, and publishes it with the bridge command or the mockup tools. A mockup is inspiration, never the spec, and never a file in the repo.

flow: the mockup offer is one more line of the single approval question on every harness (it replaces the Claude-only artifact path), asked only for a plan with a visible change and made only on the user's yes. A build reads the mockup's Keep and Free notes first, follows the project's real components before the mockup, records what it kept, adapted and dropped in the design brief and goes on. It stops to ask only when the mockup adds a feature the plan does not contain.
flow-interview, flow-critic and flow-check: the mockup wording follows the same rule.

flow, flow-task, flow-critic, flow-interview, flow-audit and flow-check: an agent never inserts tasks, steps, phases or checks on its own. It says what and why in one line, asks the user once and writes only after a yes. A request the user typed (/flow-task, a step they asked for, an interview answer) is already the confirmation. /flow-critic stays opt-in.

flow: a lite flow for plans of 1 to 3 steps (lite_new creates the item, spec and settled decisions in one call; lite_close writes the lessons, marks the last steps and releases the claim). The approval gate, step_done after each step, work_stop and every safety rule stay; the server refuses more than 3 steps.

flow: session ids no longer expire when the connector token is refreshed, and a write with an unknown id runs once under a renewed session (sessionRenewed, claimLost). step_done and record can carry sections and decisions in the same call, and a log over 500 characters is cut with a notice instead of refused.
flow: slow_calls shows the slowest MCP calls of a project to admins.

flow, flow-check and flow-verify: the limits of a check script in one list (blocked calls, the 2 minute time, writes, a signed-in registration, sample data, shared runs), proving the write path and the dialog that closes before the read-only checks, facts from the source before a check, one measurement alone, scope that stays what was asked, an answer that covers only the questions the user has seen, and a full test run on the merged tree before a push. check_save refuses a blocked script at once and can change a saved script by one edit (check_get reads it); check_status is short by default.

flow: every plan that adds or visibly changes a screen writes a design-brief section with a source on each line: the user's preferences, the brand identity, the similar components it copies, what is reused and new, and the rejected looks. A visible choice with no source copies the nearest similar component, or is asked once; it is never invented.

flow: on Claude, when its artifact tools are available, the agent asks whether the user wants a Claude artifact design mockup before asking for build approval, and makes none without a yes. Other harnesses are not asked and hear nothing about it.
flow-interview and flow-critic: both work from the design brief, and flow-critic checks its sources and that the code matches the approved mockup.

flow: a hard approval gate. Every plan ends with the approval question (build, /flow-interview, /flow-critic or change the plan) and no code, work_start or critic run happens before the user answers; the "small work needs no wait" shortcut is removed and the plan-mode critic only runs when the user chose it.
flow-check: any site may be a check target (no live-site rule, no allowlist) and the preview adopts the whole .env of the connected project with no exemption (afb-checks 1.9.0, AFB-20261022-2332).

flow-check: an app that signs in only by an emailed link gets its mail settings sealed (POSTMARK_*, with a test inbox and the owner's test-token word); the preview mails only that inbox, and a person runs login (AFB-20261022-0518).

flow, flow-check: the UI shots feature is gone (no ui_shots_run, ui_shots_get or ui_changes_save, no UI shots tab); a check's screenshots show as pictures on the item's Checks tab, so flow loses step 5b and flow-check gains a Screenshots section (AFB-20261022-2318).

Prompt diet (AFB-20261022-0217). Skip workflow_get when the skill is installed. Shared rules block removed from flow and flow-audit and shortened for the others. flow-critic size gate (1 subagent for a small diff, pass 2 only after a blocker, no question about the mode). flow: small work is plan and approval at once, critic only for 4+ steps, audit once per item, one defaults-versus-questions rule, a typed deploy request is the confirmation, no browser steps unless asked. Safety text kept once in flow and pointed to from the other skills.

UI shots capture themselves. flow: after a finished screen change call ui_shots_run with wait (step 5b), no pages and no table; flow-check: the UI shots section says the tool finds the changed screens, builds the last commit as the Before and reports plain notes. ui_changes_save only pins an extra page.

flow-check: several afb-checks registrations (repo folders) for one board project. Register the second folder with --board-project, name the registration on check_save or check_run, read runner_status registrations; a run with several registrations and none named is refused with REGISTRATION_REQUIRED and the list; project forget lets go of a registration. flow: one line in step 5a pointing at it.

flow: new Keep going rule. Once the user approves or says proceed, every phase runs to the end without stopping or asking to continue, and the only stops are a decision that is the user's, a safety rule, a tool error or a real block. A request to plan and build skips the approval wait. Questions the user's words, the code or earlier decisions can answer are decided and recorded, not asked. The same rules are in the shared workflow rules every harness gets.
flow-check: the afb-checks tool of 1.3.1 no longer carries the move from an older layout (migrate command, old credential file, checks/<item> folder); an install still on 1.2.x must be set up again.

flow-check: one afb-checks tool serves every organisation. Connecting another organisation adds a connection and never replaces one, a project is org/KEY, checks live in checks/<org>/<item>/, the worker takes several runs at once and every run has its own copy, port, browser and database. runner_status shows capacity. New run codes SANDBOX_FAILED and DOCKER_DOWN.

flow: the skills notice points at the flow_skills tool of the connection, whose reply carries the steps; the separate flow-skills skill is gone because a skill must be installed before anyone can find it, so the installer is now an MCP tool.

flow: a skillsNotice from session_start is told to the user once, with an offer to install or update the skills through the new flow_skills and skills_file tools of the MCP, on one yes without more questions (new item 7 of section 0).

flow: a step with a requiredTarget, or an automatic check, is handed to /flow-check with the item, the check key and the step (new step 5a); it is never ticked by hand without run evidence; a repo rulebook that forbids browser checks, or a user who did not ask for one, leaves it as a manual check.
flow-check: new "Called from /flow" section. flow-audit: an automatic check or requiredTarget step with no passing run is reopened.

All skills: now generic. They name no repo, path, branch, port, project key or gate command of their own. The project key is found from what the user names, the repo rulebook or board_brief; the gates come from the repo rulebook or package scripts, and when none are found the skill says so and asks.

All skills: the repo rulebook (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, README, project rules) overrides project facts and optional steps, never the safety rules: no commit or push without the user's word, no branch changes, nothing live or non-local without confirmation, no database reset, no tokens or .env values, no AI attribution.
flow-critic: every lens and lane is kept; stack-specific items now say when they apply and carry a labelled example. The subagent prompt takes a {PROJECT_DESCRIPTION} placeholder.
If your repo relied on the old built-in overrides (no UI changes table, no browser checks in plans, branch main), put them in your CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md.

flow: no usage tools any more. usage_report and the usage field of item_get are gone from the board; remove coding tool exporter env vars and the OpenCode plugin file that sent usage to the board (they now get a 404).
flow-audit, flow-check, flow-critic, flow-interview, flow-task, flow-verify: wording updates made in the same working tree, not part of the usage removal.
flow: usage_report stores a cost only when the agent passes costUsd; the board keeps no price table.
flow: names the MCP tool usage_report and item_get fields [usage], for agents whose tool exports no usage.

flow-check: rewritten for the hands-off afb-checks tool (an agent connects, repairs and upgrades it; it stops only for 5433, 5180, 5190 or a live site). Bundle 1.0.0 was never published, so its flow-check text was amended in place and keeps version 1.0.0.
First release of the system skills bundle.
